purpose: Test whether a deterministic admission gate (agent-authored fail-to-pass regression test + no-regression check, bounded retry with the gate's verdict as feedback) raises the hidden-test pass rate of a cheap coding agent. This is the product-relevant question for a harness-agnostic verify-before-accept tool.
agent: Claude Code CLI, Haiku 5.5, --effort low, 30 turns per attempt (same as exp-027)

arms.control: attempt 1 of each trajectory: same prompt plus the instruction to add a regression test; no gate feedback
arms.treatment: final attempt after up to 2 gate-rejection retries, resumed in the same session with the gate verdict

gate.G1: a new test file (name starting 'test') exists beyond the parent tree
gate.G2: the new tests exit 1 (assertion failure) on the parent source
gate.G3: the new tests pass on the patched tree
gate.G4: the existing suite (new tests ignored) passes on the patched tree; NotRun, and not blocking, if the parent suite is not green within 180 s
gate.determinism: no model call in the gate; hidden tests are never visible to the gate or the feedback

design_note: Paired within trajectory: control and treatment share attempt 1, so the contrast is exactly the effect of the gate loop. The exp-027 result (61/72 without the test-writing instruction) is reported as a reference, not as the control.
primary_outcome: paired difference in hidden-test pass rate, final minus attempt 1, with a paired bootstrap 95% interval (10000 resamples, seed 20451074)
secondary: false-admit rate: gate admits but hidden tests fail
false-reject rate: gate rejects an attempt whose hidden tests pass
success_criteria: Pass iff the paired difference is >= +4 points and the interval lower bound is > 0. Inconclusive if the lower bound <= 0 but the point estimate > 0. Fail if the point estimate <= 0. A truncated run (usage limits) is reported partial. No gate, prompt or threshold change after the first agent run; a failed gate design closes this candidate identity.
known_limits: 72 tasks give about +-11 points of sampling error on a rate; the paired contrast is tighter but still wide
the agent may also have a test-writing effect on attempt 1 itself; the paired contrast removes it from the primary outcome
the agent can see the gate rules in its prompt, which is the intended deployment
providers may have seen these public commits (dated 2025-07-01 or later)
status: Locked by ledger entry in ledgers/exp-028-admission-gate.jsonl before any agent run.
